name: Environmental Defense Fund: climate (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: shares of the result at the defaults. The public money the Inflation Reduction Act won for US households (4.6%) is in the United States; the tonnes (95.4%) spare people everywhere, spread by world population, the small US power-plant and vehicle smoke share left in the world figure.
summary: The Environmental Defense Fund (EDF; New York, with offices in Europe, China, India, Mexico, Indonesia and Japan) uses science, economics, law and advocacy for environmental policy; this model covers its climate and regional work ($120.6M in its year to September 2025, $169M with its share of core capacities) and counts the largest climate policies it worked on that were won in October 2021 to September 2025 (EPA's oil and gas methane rule, the EU Methane Regulation, the Inflation Reduction Act, EPA's power-plant and vehicle standards) and its MethaneSAT satellite, lost after 15 months, whose cost is added to the period's. At the defaults a dollar given averts about 0.0018 tonnes of CO₂e (about $560 a tonne), after the public money the Inflation Reduction Act won for US households' home rebates and credits (the recipients' gain less the taxpayers' cost, under 1%), what the law's other money costs taxpayers and the won rules' compliance costs: {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000, about two thirds of the gross tonnes from the two methane rules, whose tonnes count for methane's own, earlier warming and the ozone it forms; each win is shared with many groups and with what governments would have done anyway (EDF is credited with 2% to 25% of the advocacy behind each), the US rules and the law's credits have since been delayed, cut back or repealed. The biggest uncertainties are the shared years a won reform counts, the missing-data discount and how much of each win was advocacy's doing; every branch is discounted for missing data, since no tonne is measured for its work.

sections.title: Air pollution these tonnes carry
sections.explainer: Every tonne avoids its heat deaths; a tonne from burning less fossil fuel near people also avoids air-pollution deaths, and methane counts by its own timing and ozone. These rows say how much of the shared rates applies to EDF's tonnes (docs/normalization.md 2.5).

Inflation Reduction Act (2022): tonnes of CO₂e a year its clean-energy credits would cut by 2030, the carbon-capture credit left out
rows.explainer: The shared projection of the law's whole cut (facts: climate.ira_tco2e_per_year_2030, Princeton's REPEAT Project) less the larger carbon-capture credit's part (facts: climate.ira_45q_capture_tco2_per_year), counted as a separate win: clean power, vehicles, efficiency and the methane programme's grants. The two figures are on different bases (the capture figure is already cut to what is being built, REPEAT's projection isn't), so about 125 million tonnes of the capture credit's projected but unbuilt increment stay here before this branch's delivered share; that leaves about 0.3% of the model's value counted on a mixed basis, which we accept rather than add a second capture figure.

rows.label: MethaneSAT: oil and gas methane worldwide, tonnes of CO₂e a year
rows.explainer: The pool MethaneSAT's data could act on: the world's oil and gas operations emit about 80 million tonnes of methane a year (IEA Global Methane Tracker, 2024 and 2025 editions), 2.4 billion tonnes of CO₂e at the GWP100 of 29.8 the shared facts use. Our judgment, 2.4 billion (2.0 to 2.9), the range for the inventories' spread.

rows.label: MethaneSAT: share of that methane cut because of its data
rows.explainer: MethaneSAT measured large oil and gas regions from March 2024 until contact was lost in June 2025 and published its maps (Permian and other US basins, Central Asia, the Middle East; methane intensities two to three times the inventories in several). No regulator or company has reported a cut traced to its data; its value was to be enforcement and the EU's import rule's measurement, which the loss cut short (its aircraft, MethaneAIR, and the data already taken carry on). Our judgment, 0.02% of the world's oil and gas methane for the years below (0.002% to 0.2%), anchored on its 15 months of data from regions holding a large part of the emissions and on other satellites (TROPOMI, GHGSat, Carbon Mapper) doing much the same work.

rows.label: Share of each win due to advocacy at all (all groups together)
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: climate.advocacy_share_of_policy_win, 30%, 10% to 60%): the part of a won policy that is the advocates' doing rather than what governments, industry and events would have done. Every policy win below takes it; EDF's part of the advocates' work is each branch's attribution row. The wins are in, so this is not a chance of winning. MethaneSAT is EDF's own work and doesn't take it.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment: how far the regulators' and modellers' tonnes should be trusted
rows.explainer: The tonnes are ex-ante estimates by the regulators (EPA) and modellers (Oeko-Institut), not measured cuts; regulators' estimates of a rule's cuts are sometimes too high (compliance short of the rule) and sometimes too low (leaks larger than inventories say, as EDF's own studies found). Our judgment, 0.8 (0.5 to 1.1), applied to every branch; delivery and repeal are in each branch's implementation row.

rows.label: EU Methane Regulation: share of the tonnes that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: The shared figure for this win (50%, 20% to 85%): trade reshuffling and the US rule's overlap taken out.

rows.label: EU Methane Regulation: EDF's share of the advocacy resources behind the win
rows.explainer: EDF Europe (Brussels, London, Amsterdam) campaigned for the regulation and its import standard, and EDF's science underpins it: it led the UN Climate and Clean Air Coalition's measurement studies (note 1, p. 12) and helped design OGMP 2.0, the reporting framework the regulation adopts; EDF Europe campaigned for the import standard through the negotiations (its release on the regulation's entry into force, July 2024). Others: Clean Air Task Force, Bellona, ECOS, the Environmental Investigation Agency and many national groups, with industry lobbying on both sides. EDF's whole climate spending is large (Stabilize the Climate $99.5M and regional work $21.1M in FY2025, before core capacities and the satellite), but in Brussels its team was one of a handful, and its science counts here only as advocacy. Our judgment, 15% (5% to 30%).

source.title: EDF Europe (15 July 2024), EU launches groundbreaking methane crackdown as historic climate regulation officially enters into force
source.note: EDF Europe's statement on the regulation and its import standard; the share is our judgment.

EU Methane Regulation: share of the win's tonnes delivered
rows.explainer: The shared figure for this win (60%, 30% to 90%): the limit is not yet set and the Commission has proposed more flexibility and a delay.

rows.label: EPA methane rule: share of the tonnes that wouldn't have happened anyway
rows.explainer: The shared figure for this win (80%, 60% to 100%).

rows.label: EPA methane rule: EDF's share of the advocacy resources behind the win
rows.explainer: EDF led the field: its 16-study series with over 140 researchers (2012-2018) measured the industry's leaks at about 60% above EPA's inventory, its petitions, comments and lawsuits pushed for the rule, and it defended it in court (with others, it is suing over the 2025 delays). Others: Clean Air Task Force, NRDC, Earthjustice, Sierra Club, Earthworks, state groups and the Moms Clean Air Force (an EDF partner whose spending sits partly in these accounts); industry lobbied against parts of the rule. Our judgment, 25% (12% to 40%), the largest single share.

source.title: EDF (2025), Groups file lawsuit challenging Trump EPA final rule that delays methane pollution protections from oil and gas industry
source.note: EDF's methane studies: Alvarez et al. (2018), Assessment of methane emissions from the U.S. oil and gas supply chain, Science 361, 186-188 (emissions about 60% above EPA's inventory).

Our judgment, 60% (40% to 80%).

rows.label: Inflation Reduction Act's home rebates: recipients' gain less taxpayers' cost, units of value
rows.explainer: The law's $8.8 billion of home rebates (facts: climate.ira_home_*), the share paid to households, valued as their gain less the taxpayers' cost (docs/normalization.md 2.20) and discounted to the middle of the payouts. A fixed sum, counted once.

rows.label: Years of the larger home credits counted (the shared years a won reform counts, at most the years they paid)
Inflation Reduction Act's larger home credits: claimants' gain less taxpayers' cost, units of value
rows.explainer: The law's increase in the two home credits (25C, 25D; facts: climate.ira_home_credits_*), year by year over the years counted, valued as the claimants' gain less the taxpayers' cost and discounted from the first claims.

rows.label: Inflation Reduction Act's home rebates and credits: EDF's share of the advocacy behind them, relative to its share behind the whole law
rows.explainer: EDF and EDF Action campaigned for the bill as a whole and for its methane programme; the home rebates and credits were Rewiring America's and the solar industry's asks, so only its support for the package carries over to them: half its share of the whole law (0.2 to 1), our judgment. The tonnes keep the whole law's share: the home provisions are about 2% of them.

rows.label: Public money won for households, units of value per year of the period (after the law's branch steps)
rows.formula: (ira_rebate_uov + ira_credit_uov) * ira_attribution_share * ira_household_focus_adj * p_success * ira_counterfactual_adj * missing_data_adj / period_years
rows.explainer: The law's branch steps for the money: advocacy's share of the win, EDF's share of the advocacy behind the home provisions, what wouldn't have come anyway and the missing-data step, spread over the period's four years. The tonnes' evidence and delivery steps are left out: the money is a sum in the statute and the claims Treasury counted, its delivery in the paid share.

rows.label: Inflation Reduction Act: public money a year behind the tonnes counted here
rows.explainer: The law's energy and climate money a year (facts: climate.ira_public_cost_usd_per_year, about $65 billion) less the home rebates and credits, valued in the row above as money to households (climate.ira_household_cost_share), and less the carbon-capture credit, whose tonnes are left out here too (climate.ira_45q_capture_tco2_per_year × climate.q45_credit_usd_per_tco2).

rows.label: Inflation Reduction Act: what that money costs its payers, units of value (negative)
rows.explainer: Public money that buys tonnes is netted against what it costs those who pay for it (docs/normalization.md 2.23): the money × the value lost per dollar (row ira_payer_cost_per_dollar, on the log scale), over the same years, wait, advocacy share, counterfactual, credit, delivered share, evidence and missing-data steps as the law's tonnes, since the credits are paid per unit built.

rows.label: MethaneSAT: all adjustments combined
rows.explainer: No evidence step: MethaneSAT's cut is a judgment, not a regulator's estimate to discount.

rows.label: Share of the tonnes that wouldn't have happened anyway (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)

rows.explainer: The branches' own rows apply; this is their average, weighted by each branch's expected tonnes before adjustments, for reading only.

Share of the wins' tonnes delivered (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.formula: (eumr_downstream * eumr_counterfactual_adj * eumr_attribution_share * eumr_implementation_adj + usmeth_downstream * usmeth_counterfactual_adj * usmeth_attribution_share * usmeth_implementation_adj + pwr_downstream * pwr_counterfactual_adj * pwr_attribution_share * pwr_implementation_adj + veh_downstream * veh_counterfactual_adj * veh_attribution_share * veh_implementation_adj + ira_downstream * ira_counterfactual_adj * ira_attribution_share * ira_implementation_adj + msat_downstream * msat_counterfactual_adj * msat_attribution_share * msat_implementation_adj) / (eumr_downstream * eumr_counterfactual_adj * eumr_attribution_share + usmeth_downstream * usmeth_counterfactual_adj * usmeth_attribution_share + pwr_downstream * pwr_counterfactual_adj * pwr_attribution_share + veh_downstream * veh_counterfactual_adj * veh_attribution_share + ira_downstream * ira_counterfactual_adj * ira_attribution_share + msat_downstream * msat_counterfactual_adj * msat_attribution_share)
rows.explainer: The branches' own rows apply; this is their average, weighted by each branch's tonnes after the counterfactual and credit, for reading only.

rows.label: Other wins of the period not modelled, as a share of the modelled value
rows.explainer: The six branches are EDF's largest climate wins of the period with published tonnes, but much of the spending went elsewhere: the Inflation Reduction Act's methane fee (repealed in 2025, worth nothing now); EPA's heavy-duty truck standards (repealed with the vehicle rules); state laws (clean power and rate cases in 2025); the regional teams' work on China's carbon market and on Europe's shipping, aviation and carbon-market extension; international shipping and aviation. (Farm emissions, India's and China's included, are a branch of the health and nature model, whose accounts line pays for them.) Their spending is in the cost, so leaving them out would count them as worth nothing. Our judgment, 30% of the modelled value (10% to 80%): the modelled wins are the biggest, but the unmodelled work takes much of the climate spending.

rows.label: All adjustments combined (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.formula: (eumr_downstream * eumr_total_adj + usmeth_downstream * usmeth_total_adj + pwr_downstream * pwr_total_adj + veh_downstream * veh_total_adj + ira_downstream * ira_total_adj + msat_downstream * msat_total_adj) / (eumr_downstream + usmeth_downstream + pwr_downstream + veh_downstream + ira_downstream + msat_downstream)
rows.explainer: The branches' own combined adjustments apply; this is their average, weighted by each branch's expected tonnes before adjustments, for reading only.

Share of these tonnes that are methane
rows.formula: (eumr_expected_tonnes + usmeth_expected_tonnes + msat_expected_tonnes + ira_expected_tonnes * @climate.ira_methane_share_2030) / (eumr_expected_tonnes + usmeth_expected_tonnes + pwr_expected_tonnes + veh_expected_tonnes + ira_expected_tonnes + msat_expected_tonnes)
rows.explainer: The two methane rules' and MethaneSAT's share of the expected tonnes, weighted before waits and years counted (which can't feed a conversion row). The shared climate conversion values this share by methane's own, earlier warming and adds the ozone it forms (docs/normalization.md 2.5). The Inflation Reduction Act's methane part (facts: climate.ira_methane_share_2030) is added.

rows.label: Share of these tonnes from burning less fossil fuel near people
rows.formula: (pwr_expected_tonnes + veh_expected_tonnes + ira_expected_tonnes * (1 - @climate.ira_methane_share_2030)) / (eumr_expected_tonnes + usmeth_expected_tonnes + pwr_expected_tonnes + veh_expected_tonnes + ira_expected_tonnes + msat_expected_tonnes)
rows.explainer: Power plants and vehicles burn less fuel (the Inflation Reduction Act's tonnes are mostly clean power displacing coal and gas); methane leaks carry no fuel smoke. The act's methane part carries no fuel smoke.

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths per tonne of these fuel tonnes, relative to the fossil-fuel average
rows.explainer: Per fuel and place, weighted by expected fuel tonnes: the power-plant standards' tonnes are coal plants' (facts: climate.us_coal_power_smoke_factor); the vehicle standards' are cars' (climate.us_vehicle_smoke_factor); the Inflation Reduction Act's fuel tonnes by sector (climate.ira_power_share_2030): electricity at US power's factor (climate.us_power_smoke_factor), the rest at cars'.

rows.label: Air pollution these tonnes cut, relative to an average fossil-fuel tonne
Air-pollution deaths averted per tonne, counted directly (the US methane rule's local smog)
rows.formula: methane_share * usmeth_expected_tonnes / (eumr_expected_tonnes + usmeth_expected_tonnes + msat_expected_tonnes + ira_expected_tonnes * @climate.ira_methane_share_2030) * voc_deaths_per_year / usmeth_tonnes_per_year
rows.explainer: The US methane rule's local ozone deaths per tonne of its methane (shared figure below), × the rule's share of this model's expected tonnes, so per average tonne: they share the tonnes' credit and wait steps and are valued at the air-pollution ages by the shared conversion. The EU rule's and other methane's own ozone and earlier warming are in the shared conversion through the methane share.

rows.label: EPA methane rule: local ozone deaths a year avoided by its cut in smog-forming pollution
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: climate.us_oil_gas_methane_rule_voc_deaths_per_year): EPA's 56 (2028) to 74 (2038) local ozone deaths a year avoided by the rule's cut in volatile organic compounds near wells, as in every model that credits this rule.

rows.label: Public money won for households, in tonnes of CO₂e and the rules' compliance costs (negative)
rows.formula: uov_counted_per_year / (($deaths_per_tco2e * $climate_heat_share * ((1 - methane_share) * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -$climate_heat_death_delay + methane_share * @climate.methane_heat_deaths_vs_co2 * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -@climate.methane_heat_death_delay) * (1 + $side_effect_weight * @climate.nondeath_damages_vs_deaths) * (@death_ages.heat_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.heat_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.heat_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.heat_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74) + ($deaths_per_tco2e * (1 - $climate_heat_share) * air_pollution_weight + extra_deaths_per_tco2e + methane_share * @climate.ozone_deaths_per_tco2e_methane / (1 + ln(1 + $discount_rate) * @climate.methane_lifetime_years)) * (@death_ages.air_pollution_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74)) * $life_value_multiplier)
rows.explainer: The households' gain enters the tonnes only through the site's fixed bridge (docs/normalization.md 2.6): it moves with the value of consumption, not with the climate sliders. The won rules' compliance costs (compliance_uov_per_year) enter the same way.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO₂e averted per year of the period
rows.formula: (eumr_downstream * eumr_total_adj + usmeth_downstream * usmeth_total_adj + pwr_downstream * pwr_total_adj + veh_downstream * veh_total_adj + ira_downstream * ira_total_adj + msat_downstream * msat_total_adj) / period_years * (1 + unmodelled_benefits_adj) + tco2e_from_uov
rows.explainer: Each win's expected tonnes × its own adjustments, summed, spread over the period's four years, with the other wins added as a share, plus the public money won for households in tonnes.

EU Methane Regulation: compliance costs, units of value (negative)
rows.formula: -@compliance_costs.eu_methane_regulation_imports_cost_per_tco2e * eumr_tonnes_per_year * @cpi.usa_2024 / @cpi.usa_2018 * $uov_per_ln_consumption / (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple * @united_kingdom.consumption_per_person_2024 * @survey_consumption.survey_to_na_gbr) * eumr_downstream / eumr_tonnes_per_year * eumr_counterfactual_adj * eumr_attribution_share * eumr_implementation_adj * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The won rule's compliance costs (docs/normalization.md 2.21): the impact assessment's proxy for the import measures, exporters' abatement at $3.65 a tonne of CO₂e (2018 dollars, net of gas sold; @compliance_costs), times the import tonnes, valued as money lost by exporters' owners and EU buyers at the shared payer multiple times UK consumption per person (the site's European consumption figure); over the same years and wait as the tonnes, with the branch's chance, counterfactual, credit, delivered share and missing-data step.

rows.label: EPA oil and gas methane rule: compliance costs, units of value (negative)
rows.formula: -@compliance_costs.us_oil_gas_methane_rule_net_cost_per_year * @cpi.usa_2024 / @cpi.usa_2019 * $uov_per_ln_consumption / (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple * @united_states.ce_expenditure_per_person_2024) * usmeth_downstream / usmeth_tonnes_per_year * usmeth_counterfactual_adj * usmeth_attribution_share * usmeth_implementation_adj * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The won rule's compliance costs (docs/normalization.md 2.21): operators' net cost after the gas they recover and sell (EPA's regulatory impact analysis, $1.5 billion a year), in 2019 dollars moved to 2024's, valued as money lost by those who bear it, consumers and owners (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple, 1.2 times average US consumption), on the log scale; over the same years and wait as the rule's benefits, with the branch's chance, counterfactual, credit, delivered share and missing-data step, not its evidence adjustment (which is about the benefits).

rows.label: EPA power-plant standards: compliance costs, units of value (negative)
rows.formula: -@compliance_costs.us_power_plant_rule_2024_cost_per_year * @cpi.usa_2024 / @cpi.usa_2019 * $uov_per_ln_consumption / (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple * @united_states.ce_expenditure_per_person_2024) * pwr_downstream / pwr_tonnes_per_year * pwr_counterfactual_adj * pwr_attribution_share * pwr_implementation_adj * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The won rule's compliance costs (docs/normalization.md 2.21): the power system's extra cost (EPA's regulatory impact analysis, $0.98 billion a year), in 2019 dollars moved to 2024's, valued as money lost by those who bear it, consumers and owners (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple, 1.2 times average US consumption), on the log scale; over the same years and wait as the rule's benefits, with the branch's chance, counterfactual, credit, delivered share and missing-data step, not its evidence adjustment (which is about the benefits).

rows.label: EPA vehicle standards: compliance costs, units of value (negative)
rows.formula: -@compliance_costs.us_light_medium_vehicle_rule_2024_net_cost_per_year * @cpi.usa_2024 / @cpi.usa_2022 * $uov_per_ln_consumption / (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple * @united_states.ce_expenditure_per_person_2024) * veh_downstream / veh_tonnes_per_year * veh_counterfactual_adj * veh_attribution_share * veh_implementation_adj * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The won rule's compliance costs (docs/normalization.md 2.21): buyers' technology, charger and insurance costs less their fuel, maintenance and repair savings (EPA's rule, a net saving of $11.3 billion a year, so this row adds value), in 2022 dollars moved to 2024's, valued as money lost by those who bear it, consumers and owners (@public_funds.compliance_cost_payer_multiple, 1.2 times average US consumption), on the log scale; over the same years and wait as the rule's benefits, with the branch's chance, counterfactual, credit, delivered share and missing-data step, not its evidence adjustment (which is about the benefits).
